findings.text: Under Planning Code § 812 in force on 2022-04-20, a restaurant on the first story in CRNC was a conditional use requiring a Conditional Use Authorization from the Planning Commission.
findings.verification_note: The records show restaurant_permission as 'unknown' and do not state the requirements for restaurants in CRNC.

findings.text: Within 1,000 feet over the past 5 years, 8 of N=10 dated use decisions for this kind of business were approved (3 approved, 5 approved with conditions), 0 denied, and 2 withdrawn, for an 80% approval rate.

A 1989 CUA at this exact address (735-737 Jackson St) approved adding dim sum to an existing restaurant, and a 2005 agency referral approved a full-service restaurant as permitted; but in 2011 a small self-service restaurant application was denied with the planner noting conditional use authorization was required.

Three recent beer & wine restaurant CUAs in CRNC within 122 meters were approved with conditions limiting hours to 7am–10pm daily: 650 Jackson St (approved October 2019) and 150 Waverly Pl (approved May 2020) both received identical 7am–10pm hour restrictions.
findings.verification_note: Records show only two CUAs with these conditions, not three.

findings.text: All three nearby CUA approvals imposed standard eating and drinking conditions: sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius, soundproofing to San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance levels, odor control equipment, trash containment within the premises, and appointment of a community liaison officer.

The description does not state whether the business is part of a chain (formula retail in CRNC is not permitted for restaurants per § 812), the floor area in square feet (CRNC requires CUA for uses 2,501+ sq ft), or the closing time (principally permitted hours in CRNC end at 11pm; conditional use hours run 11pm–2am), so those triggers are not decided.
findings.verification_note: The record references § 812 but does not state the specific rules about formula retail, square footage thresholds, or operating hours.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Limited restaurant agency referral in CRNC at 1041 Stockton St, 116 meters away, approved September 2021 as a DPH referral within three months.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral approval shows that limited restaurants without alcohol can proceed through the health-department referral pathway in CRNC and be approved quickly, but this is not a CUA and does not establish conditional use entitlement for a beer & wine restaurant.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Limited restaurant agency referral in CRNC at 626 Jackson St, 140 meters away on the same block, approved July 2021 as principally permitted within one month.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral approval demonstrates that limited restaurants are principally permitted in CRNC when no alcohol is involved, but the planner's note cites Section 811 which treats restaurants with alcohol as conditional uses requiring a CUA hearing.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Withdrawn CUA at 838 Grant Ave (CVR, 153 meters away) for basement restaurant conversion, filed September 2018, withdrawn June 2019, then re-filed as 2021-008505CUA and approved.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This use decision withdrawal followed by re-application and eventual approval suggests the applicant needed to revise the proposal to address Planning concerns before winning approval; withdrawals in this area are not necessarily fatal but signal needed changes to the application.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant agency referral at 801 Kearny St in CCB district, 184 meters away, denied in August 2019 after a three-year review from June 2016 filing.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral denial demonstrates that Planning does deny restaurant applications in Chinatown when zoning or other issues are unresolved; the three-year timeline suggests protracted issues with the application that were never cured.

filing_playbook.action: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning under Planning Code §§ 303 and 812, committing to 7am–10pm daily operating hours.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the restaurant will serve beer and wine incidental to full meals (Type 41 ABC license), operate 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily, and commit to all standard eating/drinking conditions: daily sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius, soundproofing to Noise Control Ordinance standards, odor control equipment installed per approved plans, trash kept within the premises, and appointment of a community liaison officer.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Complete all remaining state and local registrations: seller's permit (CDTFA), EDD employer registration, workers' compensation insurance, fictitious business name (if the DBA differs from the entity name), and sign permit for exterior signage.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register for a seller's permit (free, issued same day online by CDTFA) before the ABC application. Register as an employer with EDD within 15 days of the first payroll. Obtain workers' comp insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund (required from the first employee). File the fictitious business name statement with the SF County Clerk if the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name, publish once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper, and file proof of publication within 45 days. Apply for a sign permit if installing new exterior signage ($300–$1,500 depending on size and illumination). Arrange ASCAP and BMI music licenses if playing recorded music or hosting live entertainment.

timeline_cost.notes: This timeline and cost range cover the four approvals in the entitlement path: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days estimated from comparable cases, not a catalog entry), ABC Type 41 license (60–120 days, $1,000–$1,600 per the ABC catalog), Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days, $470–$1,000 per the DPH catalog), and Building Permit with change of use (14–120 days, $800–$15,000 per the DBI catalog). The timeline is the time to obtain those approvals when they are granted, measured from the CUA filing to the building permit issuance and health permit issuance; it is not a time to a denial or a withdrawal. The day range assumes the CUA, ABC license, and building permit proceed in overlapping phases: file the CUA first, apply for ABC after CUA approval or in parallel, and pursue the building permit plan review while the CUA is pending, with final issuance after the CUA is granted. The cost range includes government fees only and excludes professional services (architect, expediter, attorney), construction costs, or business setup costs (entity formation, business registration, seller's permit, which total approximately $1,200–$2,000 additional). The building permit fee is a percentage of construction valuation, estimated here at $800–$15,000 for typical restaurant tenant improvements. If ABC determines the census tract is undue concentration and a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required, add 30–90 days to the ABC timeline. The health plan check ($828–$2,207) is counted separately from the building permit.
timeline_cost.path: Conditional Use Authorization (Planning Code § 303); ABC licence, Type 41 (on-sale beer and wine, eating place); Health permit to operate; Building permit with change of use

records_summary: The records show 735 Jackson St is in the Chinatown Residential Neighborhood Commercial (CRNC) district where a restaurant with beer & wine is a conditional use requiring a Planning Commission hearing. The site history reveals a 2011 denial for a small self-service restaurant at this exact address, followed by two earlier approvals (2005 full-service restaurant referral, 1989 CUA for dim sum). The immediate block is extremely dense: 49 registered food or drink businesses and 22 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 feet, with 4 bars in the count. Over the past 5 years within 1,000 feet, 8 of 10 dated use decisions were approved (80% approval rate, N=10), with 2 withdrawals and no outright denials in that window.
